verdicts.reasoning: READ: download() puts the filename into the Content-Disposition header (export/route.ts:173-182). safeFileName strips only \/:*?"<>| (export.ts:57-60). The PDF branch builds the X-Juno-Export-Notes header from unsupported strings, which are prefixed with layer names (route.ts:213; export.ts:148-205). Both are built inside the try, so a throw returns the generic 500 (route.ts:241-249). RAN on Node v26.8.1: new Response and next/server NextResponse both throw 'Cannot convert argument to a ByteString' for ホーム画面.svg, Tom’s app.svg (U+2019), 'Launch 🚀' and 'Onboarding — v2'. 'Café' works (Latin-1). SVG, PDF and HTML are affected. PNG, React, SwiftUI, tokens and handoff return JSON bodies, and json uses artifact.identifier, so those are not. The client shows the server's generic error text (design-editor.tsx:305-308).

READ: opacityAttr, rotateAttr, blendAttr and filterAttr are attached only to the node's own shape or its extra-fill group (render.ts:859-866, 935-942). Children are pushed afterwards as separate painted chunks, and the only wrapper is an optional clip group whose clipPath is not rotated either (render.ts:1024-1044). There is no layout rotation (grep of layout.ts finds none). RAN: a frame with opacity 0.5 and rotation 30 renders its child as a bare <rect> inside an unrotated clip group, while exportHtmlPrototype nests the child inside the parent div that carries opacity:0.5 and rotate(30deg). The canvas uses the same renderPageSvg (design-canvas.tsx:190-192). It is worse than claimed for groups: a group with no fill, stroke or effect has hasBox=false (render.ts:950), so its opacity, rotation and blend apply to nothing at all. The early return at opacity 0 (render.ts:814) confirms the 0 versus 0.01 discontinuity.

READ: authoring.ts:47 allows 'image'. patchFor never sets assetId (107-151), and the compact schema has no url or asset field, so no way exists to supply one. createNode then calls requireAsset(doc, undefined) and throws (operations.ts:711, 571-576). system-prompt.ts:285 lists image. RAN: normalizeDesignArtifact of a frame with an image child throws 'An image layer needs a picture'. verifyAndRepairChatArtifacts returns status 'refused'. CORRECTION: the loss is not silent in the main chat path. prepareChatArtifactOutput replaces the block with 'Artifact unavailable: verification failed, so it was not saved or presented.' and emits an 'Artifact refused' activity receipt (chat/route.ts:433-458). The artifacts-store drop at artifacts-store.ts:16-24 is a secondary guard. The whole design is still lost every time.

READ: coalesceOperations drops an earlier updateNode when its keys are a subset of the later one's (operations.ts:448). updateNode merges typography (757-759), and TypographySection sends partial typography via patchAll({typography: partial}) (inspector-panel.tsx:910). drain() coalesces each queued batch and computes `applied` from the coalesced operations (use-design-document.ts:236-247). It then adopts ackedRef and calls setDocument when the queue empties (272-280), so the size visibly reverts even on the Mac bridge, which returns no document. Only typography merges, so other fields are safe.

READ: arrangeIntoRows measures every horizontal or grid child with width=contentWidth (layout.ts:335-339). measureNode returns available.width for fill (250-256). naturalWidth then includes it, free clamps to 0, and childWidth stays at contentWidth (505-514). RAN: in a 400-wide row [A 100, B fill, C 30] with gap 10, B is at x=110 with width 400 and C is at x=520. The inspector exposes widthMode for any node (inspector-panel.tsx:233-237), and the chat prompt teaches widthMode fill. No test covers a horizontal fill child (tests/design-layout.test.ts).

READ: layout.ts:515-516 uses rowHeight for stretch or fill. Fill children are measured with height 0 (layout.ts:338). RAN: in a 400×50 horizontal row with a 20-tall sibling, both heightMode fill and alignSelf stretch come out 20 tall. The vertical branch uses contentWidth instead (layout.ts:496). For multi-row wrap or grid, row height is defensible. For the common single nowrap row in a fixed-height container it is wrong.

READ: grid rows are sliced by column count (layout.ts:348-355) and placed by the horizontal branch, which advances by each child's own width (505-520). RAN: with 2 columns, row 1 has g2 at x=110 and row 2 has g4 at x=40. It is also worse than stated: a fill child in a grid is measured at the full contentWidth (layout.ts:335-339), so every fill cell takes the whole grid width rather than one track.

READ: restorableType maps instance to frame (operations.ts:1608-1611). The deleteNodes inverse re-adds component identity only for type==='component' (806-825). componentId and overrides are not in nodePatchSchema (78-108), so fullPatchOf cannot carry them. The helper's comment claims linkage 'is re-established by the accompanying operations', but no such operations exist for instances. RAN: after deleting inst and undoing, type is frame and componentId is undefined.

READ: the inverse pushes createComponent plus setComponentProperty but not variants (operations.ts:809-824). createComponent creates variants:{} (1257-1264). deleteComponent's inverse has the same gap (1287-1291). RAN: variants were {"Size=Large":"v2"} before the delete and {} after undo. CORRECTION: the 'instances dangling' part applies only while the main stays deleted. After undo the component id exists again, but the variant map is empty.

READ and RAN: the inverse is [] for a new variant key (operations.ts:1407-1410) and for a new property (1422). CORRECTIONS: (a) Neither operation has a UI call site. grep finds createVariant and setComponentProperty only in operations.ts, instances.ts, ai.ts and a comment in inspector-panel, so only Ask Juno proposals reach them. (b) If a transaction contains only such an operation, the inverse is empty. invertTransaction then produces a zero-operation transaction, which applyTransaction rejects because designTransactionSchema requires min(1) (operations.ts:309, 355-358). So undo shows 'Couldn't undo' instead of succeeding as a no-op. In a mixed proposal (for example duplicate plus createVariant), undo removes the nodes and leaves the variant key pointing at a deleted id.

READ: ungroupNodes checks only isContainer (operations.ts:1058). Its inverse is groupNodes (1076), which builds from nodeDefaultsFor('group') (1026-1037). The context menu enables Ungroup for any container (design-context-menu.tsx:145). RAN: after ungroup and undo, the card comes back as type group with 0 fills, radius 0 and layout null. Ungrouping a component root leaves components.cmp.rootNodeId='button' pointing at a deleted node. Also, when an auto-layout frame is ungrouped, its children are re-attached using their stored x/y (which auto layout ignored) plus the group offset (1066-1069), so they jump.

READ: members are attached in operation.nodeIds order (operations.ts:1012, 1041-1047). design-editor.tsx:441 passes the selection in selection order. RAN: grouping ['button','title'] from card children [title, email, button] gives group children [button, title], so title is now painted above button.

READ: transactionIsScopedTo only filters touchedNodeIds and adds every ancestor to the allowed set without restricting which fields change (operations.ts:1682-1714). setVariableMode (1480-1491) touches no node, and neither do renameDocument, setPageBackground or createPage. The prompt says anything else is 'rejected automatically' (ai.ts:341). RAN: scoped to ['buttonLabel'], a transaction with renameDocument, setPageBackground red, createPage and updateNode on screen (width 1000, fills []) returns {ok:true}. describeChanges iterates only touched nodes (ai.ts:177-197), so the document-level changes do not appear in the review lines either.

READ: buildDocumentSummary lists only page.children as topLevel (selection-context.ts:327-342). The edit route builds selection context only when scoped (edit/route.ts:148-155). The prompt says 'CURRENT SELECTION: none.' (ai.ts:377-390) and 'Never invent an id' (ai.ts:356). Turning off the scope toggle while something is selected also sends no selection (ask-juno-bar.tsx:68, 84). CORRECTION on cost: a 422 refusal refunds the message (edit/route.ts:279). Only a returned proposal, such as a setSelection plus note answer or a re-creation, stays metered.

READ: ai.ts:298 marks id as optional, includes name, and omits kind and mimeType. assetSchema requires id, kind:'image' and mimeType, and has no name (schema.ts:544-557). The createAsset operation uses assetSchema directly (operations.ts:281). A literal-minded model therefore fails parseDesignProposal, which rejects the whole proposal. Severity lowered: the model has almost no legitimate image URL to supply, so createAsset is rarely emitted, and the failure is a refunded 422.

READ: bindVariable checks only that the variable exists (operations.ts:1465-1478). isBindable and bindablePaths have no callers outside variables.ts (grep), despite the comment at variables.ts:113-114. RAN: binding a string variable to cornerRadius passes parseDesignDocument and renders <path d="MNaN 0 HNaN VNaN HNaN VNaN Z">. Severity lowered: the only UI binding is fills.0.color, filtered to colour variables (inspector-panel.tsx:373-391), so the path is AI-only, and the preview shows the broken shape before the user accepts.

READ and RAN: layoutPage and measureNode use raw node.width and node.height (layout.ts:250-268, 401-412), and renderNode draws from the layout box (render.ts:813-816). A width bound to a 300 variable still renders width="100". CORRECTION to the scenario: a designer cannot create this binding in the UI, because the inspector binds only fills.0.color (inspector-panel.tsx:373-391). Only an AI proposal can.

READ: deleteNodes drops interactions only where the deleted node is the source (operations.ts:829-834). validateHierarchy does not look at interactions (schema.ts:598-657). The HTML runtime hides every .juno-root whose data-root is not the destination (export.ts:1197-1202). RAN: after deleting s2, interaction i1 still navigates to s2, the export contains data-navigate="s2", and unsupported is [].

READ: pdfColor uses only r, g and b (export.ts:249-251). node.opacity is used only for the ===0 early return (144). Text is split on \n only, drawn with /F1 at box.x, with no weight, family or alignment (163-175). RAN: a 10% black scrim emits '0 0 0 rg' then '0 0 300 200 re f', which is opaque black. A long paragraph in a 100-wide box is one Tj. Minor correction: the docstring promises statements only for gradients, images, paths and effects (export.ts:105-115), not 'every loss'. The silent visual damage is real either way.

READ: the regexes at export/route.ts:109 and 121 scan the whole output, including escaped text content, and escapeXml does not escape '=' or '('. RAN: a text layer 'online = true\nconst r = await fetch(url)' trips the SVG unsafe-markup check and the HTML network-call check. PNG goes through the same SVG check (route.ts:198), so it is blocked as well.

READ: POST /api/artifacts/[id] accepts any string up to 200,000 characters with no type check and no DESIGN validation (artifacts/[id]/route.ts:7-16, 40-89). canvas-panel's restore uses it (canvas-panel.tsx:420-446), and History is available for designs because hasHistory is versions.length>1 (372). The restored body carries its old revision. Any open editor at a higher revision then gets a transaction conflict and rolls back, which clears its undo stack (use-design-document.ts:198-208). Related and worse: see the missed defect about empty placeholder versions.

READ: loadOwnedDesignArtifact includes every version with its content (store.ts:34-37). appendVersion and rewriteVersion include them again (163-166, 193-196). The transactions, edit, export and GET routes all call loadOwnedDesignArtifact. rewriteVersion's compare-and-swap also sends the full old body as a WHERE predicate (185-188). A new checkpoint is allocated once the newest row is 30 s old (operations.ts:511, 529-539). The 18 MB figure is an inference from those numbers.

READ: the refine accepts any URL starting with '/' (schema.ts:553), so '//host/p.png' passes. The web canvas injects the SVG inline (design-canvas.tsx:1078), and the web CSP allows img-src https: (csp.ts:39). The export check rejects non-/api/files URLs (export/route.ts:86). CORRECTION: the Mac and iPhone bundled editor is not affected. Its CSP is img-src 'self' data: (native/macOS/JunoDesktop/Resources/DesignEditor/index.html:16). The leak is web-only.

READ: grep of export.ts:1347-1650 finds no handling of strokes (apart from the glass rim), fontFamily, letterSpacing, lineHeight, textAlign, italic, clipsContent or blendMode. The font is always .system(size:weight:) (line 1467). RAN: a frame with a 2 pt red inside stroke and centred Georgia text exports with no stroke, .system font and .topLeading alignment, and unsupported=[].

READ and RAN: HTML and React output contain no white-space, box-sizing, verticalAlign or mix-blend rules (grep of export.ts finds none). The HTML text 'Line 1\nLine 2' is emitted raw, and React emits {"Line 1\nLine 2"}; both collapse to one line. An inside 2 pt stroke becomes 'border: 2px solid' on a 200px content-box element, so it renders 204 wide and shifts children by the border width.

READ: descendant mappings use line: lines.length after the component's closing lines have been pushed (export.ts:1324, 1631), while roots use lines.length+1 at the start. RAN: SwiftUI maps t and r to line 30 of a 30-line split, and React maps them to line 12 of 12, i.e. the trailing end of the file. findSymbol consumers get the wrong line.

READ: normalizeDesignArtifact sends any schemaVersion>0 to parseDesignDocument (authoring.ts:223-225). designDocumentSchema allows up to 1000 (schema.ts:564). migrateDesignDocument refuses versions above the current one (migrations.ts:65-69). The chat verification step uses the same normalizer (chat-artifact-verification.ts:92), so it would pass. This is unlikely in practice: the prompt forbids full documents with schemaVersion (system-prompt.ts:291), and the model would have to write an otherwise fully valid document.

READ: validateDesignAssets iterates every asset in doc.assets and runs before the format switch (export/route.ts:66-102, 162-163), so json, tokens and handoff exports, and layer exports, are blocked too. deletedAt!=null makes it return MISSING_ASSET (89-93).

READ: .slice(0, 2_000) at route.ts:213. The client saves the blob first and then runs JSON.parse on the header, catching errors into toast.error (design-editor.tsx:329-341). RAN: 60 rounded rects with names produce a 4,731-character notes string, and parsing the 2,000-character slice throws 'Unterminated string in JSON at position 2000'.

READ: store.ts:48-51 falls back to versions.at(-1), and route.ts:24-28 only checks for a positive integer. CORRECTION: the defect is latent. No client in src or native calls GET /api/design/[id]?version= (grep for 'api/design' finds only /api/design creation, transactions, edit and export callers). The history viewer scenario does not exist; the canvas History uses artifact versions from the generic artifact API. It remains an API contract bug.

READ: design-editor.tsx:436-442 returns when selection.length < 2, before the shift branch, so ⇧⌘G on a single group does nothing. The context menu advertises ⇧⌘G and enables Ungroup for a single container (design-context-menu.tsx:145, 265-270).

Same mechanism as web-design-model-1, reproduced in Node. The client shows the server's generic 'Export failed. Please try again.' (route.ts:249; design-editor.tsx:305-308), and nothing tells the user the name is the cause. Scope: SVG, PDF and HTML downloads only. PNG, React, SwiftUI, tokens, handoff and JSON are JSON responses or use the ASCII identifier. The claim that such names are common is an inference (the model-written titles in system-prompt examples use plain ASCII).

Same as web-design-model-14. The unscoped placeholder is just 'Ask Juno to change this design…' (ask-juno-bar.tsx:199-205), with no hint to select a layer. The prompt allows a setSelection plus note answer (ai.ts:362), which the bar shows as a note (ask-juno-bar.tsx:88-91).

READ: maxDuration is 120 (edit/route.ts:22). Provider text is buffered into `raw` and a single JSON response is returned (186-201, 256-271). includeImage is false, and the prompt is text-only (150-155). The UI has only a spinning send key (ask-juno-bar.tsx:217-234) and no cancel control; abort happens only on unmount (66). CORRECTION: DESIGN_TOOLS (ai.ts:256-270) is an exported constant with no references anywhere (grep). It is not sent to the model or shown to users, so it 'advertises' nothing. It is dead code describing a loop that does not exist.

READ: MAX_IMAGE_BYTES is 96 KB, inlined as a data URL, which is about 131K base64 characters (use-design-document.ts:569-588). The store refuses documents over 200,000 characters with 'This change would make the document too large to save.' (store.ts:63, 117-120), and the client rolls back the whole queued batch (use-design-document.ts:198-208, 265-270). No size meter or warning exists in src/components/design (grep for 200_000, budget and too-large). There is no UI path to non-inlined /api/files assets (grep finds none), even though export supports them.

The core claim is confirmed (see web-design-model-3; probe refused). CORRECTION: the drop is not 'only a server log line'. The chat route replaces the block with 'Artifact unavailable: verification failed, so it was not saved or presented.' and sends an 'Artifact refused' activity with the reason (chat/route.ts:433-458). The user does learn that something failed but still loses the whole design, and the prompt that caused it recommends image nodes.

Same as web-design-model-2, reproduced: the canvas and SVG leave children at full opacity and unrotated, while the HTML export nests them under the faded, rotated parent. It is worse for plain groups, which have no box to carry opacity or rotation, so those settings do nothing on the canvas.

missed.title: Chat Canvas design editor remounts on an empty placeholder version after the first new checkpoint; restoring such a version writes an empty design
missed.evidence: READ (not run): onCommitted appends { version, content: "" } to artifact.versions and bumps currentVersion (canvas-panel.tsx:1243-1254). An effect then sets selectedVersion = artifact.currentVersion (313-315). versionContent = versions.find(v => v.version === selectedVersion)?.content ?? artifact.content, and "" is not nullish, so it returns "" (369-370). The DesignEditor wrapper is keyed by selectedVersion and fed content={versionContent} (1236-1240), and useDesignDocument parses initialContent on mount (use-design-document.ts:169-188); JSON.parse("") fails with 'Design document is not valid JSON'. The first user edit on a chat-generated design always allocates a new checkpoint (allocatesCheckpoint returns true when latest.origin !== 'edit', operations.ts:529-539), and the transactions route returns the new currentVersion (transactions/route.ts:53-54; use-design-document.ts:100-103). handleArtifactUpdated stores the placeholder version in chat state (chat-view.tsx:1254-1262). Separately, History restore posts targetEntry.content (canvas-panel.tsx:385, 445) through the generic route, which accepts "" (artifacts/[id]/route.ts:8), so restoring an in-session checkpoint stores an empty, unreadable design body.
missed.failure_scenario: A user opens a chat-made design in the Canvas panel and moves a layer. The save creates v2. The panel re-keys the editor to v2, whose client-side content is "", and the design is replaced by 'Design document is not valid JSON' until the conversation is reloaded. If the user instead opens History, picks that in-session version and presses Restore, the server stores an empty body and every design route returns 422 for that artifact until the user restores an older version.

missed.title: Group opacity, rotation and blend mode have no visible effect on the canvas or in SVG/PNG
missed.evidence: hasBox is false for a group with no fills, stroke, filter or surface (render.ts:950). The group's opacityAttr, rotateAttr and blendAttr exist only on that box markup via `common` (935). The children are rendered unwrapped (1028-1031). The inspector and the operations accept opacity and rotation on groups (nodePatchSchema, operations.ts:78-108).
missed.failure_scenario: A designer sets a group to 30% opacity or rotates it 15°. Nothing changes on the canvas or in SVG/PNG export. In HTML/React/SwiftUI the group is faded or rotated.
